criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md has a bullet saying that when a request touches CI caching or CI speed, the reading states how the GitHub Actions cache is scoped by branch and puts that constraint in an acceptance criterion.
criteria.evidence: I read reader.md. The wording is there, but it is not a bullet. Line 7 reads "- Name the goal and audience (who uses the result) in the summary or assumptions.- For CI caching or CI speed, state in an acceptance criterion how the GitHub Actions cache is scoped by branch: ...". The newline before "- For CI" is missing, so the rule sits at the end of the goal/audience bullet. It renders as one list item, and readers of the raw prompt see it as one item too.

criteria.criterion: The bullet states the scoping correctly: a run restores caches from its own branch (or PR merge ref), its base branch, and the default branch; it cannot restore caches from sibling or unrelated branches; caches saved by a feature branch are not visible to the default branch or other branches.
criteria.evidence: I read the text: "runs restore only from their own branch (or PR merge ref), base branch and the default branch, never sibling branches; feature-branch caches are invisible to the default branch and others." This covers all three points of the criterion and matches GitHub's documented cache restore rules.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs asserts READER_FRAME.text names the CI cache, branch scoping, base/default branch and acceptance criterion. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: it passes, and it would fail if the bullet were removed.
criteria.evidence: The new test reader_names_the_github_actions_cache_branch_scoping_for_ci_work checks five substrings of READER_FRAME.text, and it passes (123 passed). I could not remove the rule to watch the test fail, because this role changes nothing. By reading the file, each of the five substrings appears only in the new rule text, so removing it would make the test fail.

criteria.criterion: The reader token budget is unchanged at 2000 (BudgetSet::Reader in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs); existing wording is tightened so the existing budget tests still pass. Run `cargo test -p athena-context` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`.
criteria.evidence: The diff does not touch BudgetSet::Reader. Both test runs pass: athena-context 123 passed, budgets 5 passed, including every_role_set_is_within_its_budget and system_facts_budgets_match_computed. The reader set is now at 1999 of 2000.

criteria.criterion: No other prompt set exceeds its budget and the whole workspace is healthy. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (clean) and `cargo fmt --check`.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for 731ecd47 passed: fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and the full test suite. These results come from CI run 42434165680. The budgets test every_role_set_is_within_its_budget also passed in my run.

criteria.criterion: Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) are not changed; the existing guidance in reader.md is trimmed only in wording, not in meaning.
criteria.evidence: No governance file changed. But the trimming dropped meaning in four places. (1) The sentence "Read existing output first." was deleted from the goal/audience bullet. (2) "the job runs on your assumption unless answered" became "the job proceeds on it": "unless answered" is lost, and "it" is unclear. (3) "records/, private files, and history are absent by design" became "a copy lacking records/, private files, and history": "by design", which tells the reader the gap is intended, is lost. (4) "Always give one complete reading" lost "Always".

findings.summary: The new rule is joined onto the previous bullet instead of being its own bullet.
findings.evidence: reader.md line 7: "...in the summary or assumptions.- For CI caching or CI speed, state in an acceptance criterion...". The newline is missing, which breaks the bullet list. The reader set is at 1999 of 2000 tokens, so the newline was most likely dropped to save a token. Fix: restore the newline and make room by tightening other wording.

findings.summary: Trimming reader.md removed guidance, not just words, which criterion 6 does not allow.
findings.evidence: Deleted outright: "Read existing output first." Weakened: "the job runs on your assumption unless answered" became "the job proceeds on it". Dropped: "absent by design" for records/. Dropped: "Always" in "Always give one complete reading".

findings.summary: Soundness: the change fits the budget by deleting a newline and existing guidance, when it should have found a real wording saving.
findings.evidence: A careful reviewer would reject saving a token by gluing two bullets together and cutting a rule ("Read existing output first."). The better approach is to tighten wording elsewhere that does not change meaning, or to say the budget cannot hold the rule and send it back to the user.

summary: The new rule states the GitHub Actions cache scoping correctly, the new test passes, and all budgets and workspace checks pass. The verdict is still fail, for two reasons. First, the rule is not its own bullet. The newline before it was dropped, so in reader.md line 7 it is glued onto the end of the previous bullet ("...in the summary or assumptions.- For CI caching..."). This was most likely done to save a token under the 2000-token budget. Second, the trimming dropped meaning, not just words. "Read existing output first." is gone completely. "the job runs on your assumption unless answered" became "the job proceeds on it", which loses "unless answered". The note that records/ are "absent by design" is gone. That breaks criterion 6, which allows trimming wording only. Smaller issues: two files outside the deliverables list changed. docs/system-facts.md had to change, because a test checks it. docs/design/context-engineer.md did not have to change, and the edit rewrote a measured evidence figure in that doc.
